simple: UI (user interface) is everything players see and click that is not the 3D world itself: health bars, shop menus, buttons, name tags, and more. This page is a map of all the UI tools Roblox gives you. UI can sit flat on the player's screen or live inside the 3D world, like a sign on a wall. Most UI is built from a few basic pieces: frames, labels, buttons, and text boxes.
analogy: Building UI is like making a poster with stickers: frames are the boards, labels are the text and pictures you stick on, and buttons are stickers you can press.
keyPoints: On-screen UI goes in a `ScreenGui` and shows on the player's screen; it lives and runs on the player's device (the client).
In-world UI uses a `SurfaceGui` (stuck to a part's face) or a `BillboardGui` (floats and always faces the camera).
`Frame` holds other UI, `TextLabel`/`ImageLabel` show text or pictures, `TextButton`/`ImageButton` can be clicked, and `TextBox` lets players type.
`Position`, `Size`, `AnchorPoint`, and `ZIndex` control where UI goes, how big it is, and what sits on top.
Tweening smoothly animates UI from one look or spot to another.
Layouts like `UIListLayout` and grids line items up for you, and modifiers like `UIStroke` and `UIGradient` add outlines and color fades.
Universal styling lets you set looks in one place and apply them everywhere, a bit like CSS on websites.
Proximity prompts, UI drag detectors, and 3D drag detectors add ready-made ways for players to interact.

terms.UI / GUI: User interface or graphical user interface. The menus, buttons, and text on top of or inside your game.
terms.GuiObject: Any 2D UI piece you can place, such as a frame, label, button, or text box.
terms.container: An object that holds UI so it can be shown, like `ScreenGui`, `SurfaceGui`, or `BillboardGui`.
terms.client: The player's own device (computer, phone, console). On-screen UI is handled there, not on the server.
terms.AnchorPoint: The spot on a UI object that its `Position` refers to. (0, 0) is the top-left corner; (0.5, 0.5) is the center.
terms.ZIndex: A number that decides which UI is drawn on top. A higher ZIndex covers a lower one.
terms.tweening: Smoothly changing a property over time, like sliding a menu in over 0.5 seconds instead of popping it in.
terms.stylesheet: A list of style rules (colors, fonts, sizes) you write once and apply to lots of UI.

watchOut: On-screen UI is controlled by the client, so change it from a `LocalScript`, not a server `Script`.
Do not cram everything into one big frame. Use frames and layouts to keep UI tidy and easy to move.
Remember players use phones too. Test your UI in different screen sizes.
